blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

items.t: "West Meadows" is the MLS® sub-area name for the part of the City of Pitt Meadows west of Harris Road: the Pitt Meadows Regional Airport (YPK) lands, large farm parcels along Ford Road, Fraser Way and Airport Way, and the Pitt River and Fraser River shorelines. It is not an official City neighbourhood name, and no official City planning-area name for the west side was found in City sources. Working limits only: Harris Road to the east, the Pitt River to the west and north-west, the Fraser River to the south, and Lougheed Highway to the north — exact limits: Not verified.

Where the condo stock concentrates: nowhere in this sub-area —. The land pattern explains it: the main zones are A-1 General Agriculture and A-2 Large Lot Agricultural, with a small detached-house pocket (Fraser Way / Wildwood Crescent) at the east edge under RS and R-3/R-4/R-6 residential zones. The city's condo corridor begins east of Harris Road, in Central and Mid Meadows.

What is actually in the sub-area: Pitt Meadows Regional Airport (YPK) at 1028-18799 Airport Way — three paved runways and a water runway, owned and operated by the Pitt Meadows Airport Society; Harris Landing at Harris Road and Fraser Way, the start of the Pitt River Greenway (about 10.2 km of dike-top trail along the Fraser and Pitt rivers); Fraser Way Roundabout Park at 19501 Fraser Way. No recreation centre, library branch or public school building sits inside the sub-area.

Davie Jones Elementary, 12030 Blakely Rd; Edith McDermott Elementary, 12178 Bonson Rd; Highland Park Elementary, 18961 Advent Rd (all K–7), plus Pitt Meadows Secondary, 19438 116b Ave (Grades 8–12) — because the area has no official boundary, so it cannot place a school inside it. SD42 catchments are address-based with no middle tier; the recorded locator run for 19452 Fraser Way returned Davie Jones Elementary and Pitt Meadows Secondary.

blocks.text: Good to know about West Meadows

items.t: The City's 2020 Business Plan says over 95% of Pitt Meadows is floodplain. The current figure is "over 95%" — quote it and cite the Business Plan.
West Meadows is an airport and farm sub-area wearing a residential name. A buyer searching West Meadows for condos is searching the wrong sub-area; the condo corridor starts across Harris Road.

78% of the city is farmland, and this sub-area is where much of it sits. The 2020 Business Plan puts 78% of Pitt Meadows in the Agricultural Land Reserve, and this sub-area's A-1 subdivision minimum is 8 ha (A-2: 16 ha) — which is why there is no condo supply here and none is planned in the OCP's agriculture-dominant framework.

Farm-class taxes are an order of magnitude different. Under Bylaw No. 3047, 2026 the Farm class general rate is $48.6824 per $1,000 against the residential general rate of $2.8438 per $1,000 — a carrying-cost fact that surprises acreage buyers who budget from residential Pitt Meadows figures.

The dike trail starts at the condo corridor's doorstep. Harris Landing, at Harris Road and Fraser Way, is the start of the Pitt River Greenway — about 10.2 km west along the Fraser and Pitt River dikes for walking, cycling and bird watching — so the trail amenity marketed to Harris Road condo buyers runs through this sub-area, not theirs.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in West Meadows
Streets, schools and getting around West Meadows

items.t: West Meadows is the part of the City of Pitt Meadows west of Harris Road: the Pitt Meadows Regional Airport (YPK) lands, large farm parcels along Ford Road, Fraser Way and Airport Way, and the Pitt River and Fraser River shorelines.

No official boundary is published. Working limits only: Harris Road to the east, the Pitt River to the west and north-west, the Fraser River to the south, and Lougheed Highway to the north, taking in Airport Way, Ford Road and the west end of Fraser Way; exact limits of the MLS sub-area are not confirmed. Nearby areas: Central Meadows to the east across Harris Road, Mid Meadows to the south-east, North Meadows across Lougheed Highway, and Port Coquitlam across the Pitt River.

Where the homes actually sit: farm houses on large A-1 / A-2 agricultural parcels along Ford Road and Airport Way, plus detached houses in the Fraser Way / Wildwood Crescent pocket at the east edge under the RS, R-3, R-4 and R-6 residential zones. There is no verified townhouse node inside the board's West Meadows reading.

Transit and roads: TransLink route 722 (Bonson / Meadowtown) runs via Harris Road and Ford Road, then Hammond Road, Bonson Road and Fraser Way, continuing as route 719; routes 701 and 791 and the R3 Lougheed Hwy RapidBus connect at Pitt Meadows Station, and the West Coast Express runs weekday trains from Pitt Meadows Station to Waterfront Station. Airport Way, Ford Road, Fraser Way and Harris Road serve the area; Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) runs along the north edge.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in West Meadows

items.t: Short-term rentals are prohibited in Pitt Meadows: a City staff report to Council (October 23, 2024, for the November 5, 2024 meeting) states it plainly — "Short-Term Rentals: Short-term rental accommodation is not a permitted use in Zoning Bylaw" — and the proposed amendment was to clarify that prohibition and distinguish the use from other permitted uses. Separately, the Province's principal-residence requirement lists Pitt Meadows among the communities where it applies. A West Meadows (or any Pitt Meadows) townhouse business plan built on short-term rental income fails at the zoning bylaw, before any strata bylaw is read.

Floodplain — the city's defining land rule: the city is almost entirely protected by 60 km of dikes, plus ditches, pump stations and flood boxes; A-1 zoning requires residential buildings sited 15.0 m from watercourses, key ditches and constructed ditches, and the Kennedy drainage area (Area 3) in this part of the city discharges to the Alouette, Pitt and Fraser Rivers.

Form B diligence (applies to the strata townhouses a West Meadows buyer will actually meet — Shoreline and Coho II, filed under South Meadows): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. There is no in-area strata stock to apply it to.

blocks.text: Good to know about West Meadows

items.t: The airport is inside the sub-area, not beside it: Pitt Meadows Regional Airport (YPK), at 1028-18799 Airport Way, has three paved runways and a water runway and is owned and operated by the Pitt Meadows Airport Society — disclose aircraft activity early and use the City's airport page for the noise-concern process rather than discovering it at subject removal.

Harris Landing, at Harris Road and Fraser Way, is the start of the Pitt River Greenway — about 10.2 km west along the Fraser and Pitt River dikes for walking, cycling and bird watching, with the Metro Vancouver Pitt River Regional Greenway following the dike tops between Kennedy Road and Ford Road.

78% of the city is in the Agricultural Land Reserve (City 2020 Business Plan), and A-1 subdivision minimum is 8 ha — the single most common West Meadows pricing error is valuing a farm parcel as if it could be split like a suburban lot.

Golden Ears Way is being widened from two lanes to four between the Highway 7 interchange and 210 Street under a TransLink / City of Maple Ridge design agreement — the corridor change that will most affect this area's commutes, on the record before it is built.

The nearest hospital is in the next city: Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, Maple Ridge (Fraser Health), with 24/7 emergency care serving Maple Ridge and Pitt Meadows; the Ridge Meadows Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at 121-11900 Haney Place, Maple Ridge.

No recreation centre or library branch sits inside the sub-area either: the Pitt Meadows Family Recreation Centre is at 12027 Harris Road and the city's only library branch is Pitt Meadows Public Library, 200-12099 Harris Road — both just east of Harris Road, in Central Meadows.

blocks.text: Lots and land in West Meadows
Fee-simple farm parcels

items.t: Farm parcels along Ford Road, Airport Way and Fraser Way: farm houses on large agricultural parcels under A-1 General Agriculture and A-2 Large Lot Agricultural zoning, the main zones in the sub-area. A-2 protects large-lot farming areas under regulations consistent with the Agricultural Land Commission Act.

Lot character from the zones, as the bylaw states it: A-1 allows one farm house per lot (maximum gross floor area 500 m²), one additional farm house for farm operations over 8 ha and under 40 ha, and two if 40 ha or more. These are zone rules, not a claim about any existing parcel's size.

ALR vs non-ALR, as documented: the City's 2020 Business Plan states 78% of Pitt Meadows land falls within the ALR; the large farm parcels in this sub-area are zoned A-1 / A-2 under rules consistent with the Agricultural Land Commission Act, and a specific property's ALR status is confirmed on ALC maps. No finer West Meadows-specific ALR percentage is stated.

Servicing — the farm-parcel check: septic and well servicing details for individual farm parcels are not verified; wells are checkable in the provincial Groundwater Wells and Aquifers (GWELLS) application, and a home not connected to a community sewer must have an onsite system complying with the Sewerage System Regulation. Do not assume urban servicing on A-1 / A-2 ground.
Siting: A-1 zoning requires residential buildings sited 15.0 m from watercourses, key ditches and constructed ditches — a buildable-envelope constraint on ditch-crossed farm parcels.

Flood position: over 95% of the city land base is in the Fraser / Pitt floodplain behind 60 km of dikes, plus ditches, pump stations and flood boxes (City 2020 Business Plan — governing figure; the Kennedy drainage area (Area 3) in this part of the city discharges to the Alouette, Pitt and Fraser Rivers.

Airport ground is not lot inventory: Pitt Meadows Regional Airport (YPK), at 1028-18799 Airport Way inside this sub-area — three paved runways and a water runway, owned and operated by the Pitt Meadows Airport Society — is operating airport land, documented here as the sub-area's dominant land use neighbour, never as for-sale land. No airport noise-zone map covering the sub-area was verified (research not verified item).

blocks.text: Fee-simple house lots

items.t: Fraser Way / Wildwood Crescent pocket: detached houses at the area's east edge under RS Large Lot Residential (minimum lot area 0.2 ha) and R-3 / R-4 / R-6 Urban Residential (up to 3, 4 or 6 units per lot; R-6's sixth unit conditional on an adaptable unit; subdivision minimum 1,215 m²). Secondary suites and garden suites are listed accessory uses in the RS zone (one garden suite per lot at 33–90 m²; a lot cannot have both a garden suite and a secondary suite).

items.t: West Meadows is the part of the City of Pitt Meadows, BC, in Metro Vancouver, west of Harris Road: the Pitt Meadows Regional Airport (YPK) lands, large farm parcels along Ford Road, Fraser Way and Airport Way, and the Pitt River and Fraser River shorelines.

Boundaries: no official boundary is published. Nearby: Central Meadows to the east across Harris Road, Mid Meadows to the south-east, North Meadows across Lougheed Highway to the north, and Port Coquitlam across the Pitt River to the west.

Main roads and transit: Airport Way, Ford Road, Fraser Way and Harris Road serve the area; Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) runs along the north edge, and Golden Ears Way / Golden Ears Bridge connects north toward Maple Ridge and south to Langley and Surrey. Route 722 runs via Harris Road and Ford Road on its west-side segment, continuing as route 719; routes 701, 791, the R3 RapidBus and the West Coast Express connect at Pitt Meadows Station and the Harris Road stop on Lougheed Highway, east of the area.

Civic anchors: Harris Landing, at Harris Road and Fraser Way, is the start of the Pitt River Greenway (about 10.2 km west along the Fraser and Pitt River dikes); Fraser Way Roundabout Park is at 19501 Fraser Way. No recreation centre, library branch, shopping centre or grocery store inside the sub-area was verified — the Family Recreation Centre (12027 Harris Road) and the city's only library branch (200-12099 Harris Road) sit just east of Harris Road, and the nearest confirmed shopping is Meadowtown (19800 Lougheed Highway, Real Canadian Superstore) and Meadowvale (Harris Road, Save-On-Foods). Nearest hospital: Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, Maple Ridge.

Schools: no public school building is located inside this sub-area on the district list. SD42 catchments are address-based and SD42 has no middle-school tier — elementary K–7, secondary 8–12. That sample result does not transfer to other addresses.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in West Meadows

items.t: ALR rules — the core land rules in this sub-area: Note the zoning layer differs in form (A-1 additional farm houses for farm operations over 8 ha —): a farm-residence thesis must satisfy both the ALC caps and the A-1 rules.
Farm class — three-tier, never flat: Farm-class status drives the tax picture below, so confirm the parcel's class and production position before quoting carrying costs.

Property taxes — read the bill by class: under the 2026 Annual Tax Rates Bylaw No. 3047, 2026 (adopted May 5, 2026), the Farm class (Class 9) general rate is $48.6824 per $1,000 with a $1.8524 drainage levy, versus Class 1 Residential at $2.8438 general and $0.1082 drainage — confirm the property's BC Assessment class before quoting carrying costs on any farm parcel. Taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after August 1, 2026.

blocks.text: Good to know about West Meadows

items.t: Ford Road is two sub-areas at once: MLS sources class Ford Road addresses near 122 Avenue as Central Meadows, while the road's south-west reach reads as West Meadows farm country — and the Ford Road co-op's own board sub-area is not confirmed from public sources.

The tax class is the carrying-cost story: the 2026 Farm class general rate ($48.6824/$1,000) is roughly seventeen times the residential rate ($2.8438/$1,000) in the same bylaw — losing or never having farm class on a West Meadows parcel changes the holding math more than any other single line. Confirm class with BC Assessment before quoting costs.

A water runway, not just pavement: YPK's water runway on the river side makes this one of the few BC sub-areas where floatplane traffic is part of the soundscape — worth a site visit at a busy hour before buying in the Fraser Way pocket.
It is not in West Meadows and contributes nothing here; recorded only so the name is never mis-filed on age or geography.

The ground in West Meadows

items.t: The farm parcels: Farm houses on large agricultural parcels along Ford Road and Airport Way under A-1 General Agriculture and A-2 Large Lot Agricultural zoning, the main zones in the sub-area. A-1: one farm house per lot (maximum gross floor area 500 sq m), one additional farm house allowed for farm operations over 8 ha and under 40 ha (two if 40 ha or more), minimum lot area for subdivision 8 ha. A-2: protects large-lot farming areas under regulations consistent with the Agricultural Land Commission Act; minimum lot area for subdivision 16 ha. A-1 siting requires residential buildings 15.0 m from watercourses, key ditches and constructed ditches. These are zone rules, not a claim about any existing parcel's size — a specific parcel's area, zone and ALR status are confirmed on title and ALC maps. The east-edge residential pocket: detached houses in the Fraser Way / Wildwood Crescent pocket under RS Large Lot Residential (minimum lot area 0.2 ha) and R-3 / R-4 / R-6 Urban Residential (up to 3, 4 or 6 units per lot; R-6's sixth unit is conditional on an adaptable unit; subdivision minimum 1,215 sq m).

Strata position: predominantly freehold, and no strata stock at all in the data: The Fairways (Pitt Meadows) is verified condo stock on North Meadows ground in the city assembly, with its age position not confirmed — it is never called 55+ and is not West Meadows stock.

Serviced vs unserviced: septic and well servicing details for individual farm parcels: Not verified — wells are checkable in the provincial Groundwater Wells and Aquifers (GWELLS) application, and a home not connected to a community sewer must have an onsite system complying with the Sewerage System Regulation. No parcel is described as serviced, on a well, or on septic from a summary.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect duplexes in West Meadows

items.t: Secondary suites and garden suites are listed accessory uses in the RS zone; the City garden suite guide sets one suite per lot at 33 to 90 sq m, and a lot cannot have both a garden suite and a secondary suite. On ALR land the Agricultural Land Commission allows one additional detached residence without an application where there is one existing residence when construction begins, to a maximum of 90 sq m on properties 40 ha or less.

Flood / dikes / ALR / airport: The City is almost entirely protected by 60 km of dikes, plus ditches, pump stations and flood boxes; the Kennedy drainage area (Area 3) in this part of the city discharges to the Alouette, Pitt and Fraser Rivers, and zoning siting in A-1 requires residential buildings 15.0 m from watercourses, key ditches and constructed ditches. ALR: 78% of Pitt Meadows land falls within the ALR per the same Business Plan; the large farm parcels here are zoned A-1 / A-2 under rules consistent with the Agricultural Land Commission Act, and a specific property's ALR status is confirmed on ALC maps: Not verified at parcel level. Airport: Pitt Meadows Regional Airport (YPK) is inside this sub-area at 1028-18799 Airport Way — three paved runways and a water runway, owned and operated by the Pitt Meadows Airport Society; the City maintains a page for safety and noise concerns; an official airport noise-zone map covering this sub-area is not verified.

faq.a: No verified ones. The city's named condo buildings — Solaris at Meadows Gate, Origin, Liv42, Orion, Cedar Downs — are all on or east of Harris Road in Central and Mid Meadows.
faq.q: Are there any condos in West Meadows?

faq.a: The address. Harris Road is this sub-area's east edge, and the Harris Road condo corridor (12069, 11950, 12409, 12350 Harris Road) sits in Central and Mid Meadows in the city-wide assignment.
faq.q: A listing says "West Meadows" but the address is on Harris Road — which is right?

faq.a: A townhome pocket exists along Fraser Way west of Harris Road, but no complex name was confirmed on an official, developer or strata source — name not verified. Any purchase there is a townhome strata purchase: Form B, depreciation report (if 5+ lots), CRF position and the registered bylaws are the diligence set.
faq.q: What about the townhomes on Fraser Way?

faq.a: No. Short-term rental accommodation is not a permitted use under Pitt Meadows' Zoning Bylaw at all — the ban is city-wide and does not depend on strata bylaws — and the Province's principal-residence requirement also lists Pitt Meadows. Long-term rental of a strata unit is a different question; strata rental bylaws are void since November 24, 2022.
faq.q: Can I run an Airbnb or short-term rental here?

faq.a: Protection is a 60 km dike system plus ditches, pump stations and flood boxes, funded in part by the separate drainage levy on the tax bill.
faq.q: How much of this area is floodplain, and what protects it?

faq.a: There is no verified townhouse complex inside the board's West Meadows.
faq.q: Where are the West Meadows townhouses, actually?

faq.a: No. Short-term rental accommodation is not a permitted use in the City's Zoning Bylaw — the City states the prohibition expressly — and the provincial principal-residence requirement also applies in Pitt Meadows.
faq.q: Can I run an Airbnb in a Pitt Meadows townhouse?

faq.a: It is not a purchase of title at all: the Ford Road Housing Co-operative is membership housing (apartments plus 3–4 bedroom townhouses) — no strata lot, no fee-simple lot, nothing to resell as real estate. It is also not a 55+ building.
faq.q: Is the Ford Road co-op a way to buy a townhouse here cheaply?

faq.a: Not verified per parcel — check wells in the provincial GWELLS application and confirm any onsite sewerage system complies with the Sewerage System Regulation before offering.
faq.q: Is a farm parcel serviced, on a well, or on septic?

faq.a: A-1 homes must also sit 15.0 m from watercourses and ditches. Verify the specific parcel with the City.
faq.q: Is West Meadows in a floodplain?

faq.a: No — short-term rental accommodation is not a permitted use in Pitt Meadows' Zoning Bylaw, and the city is in the Province's principal-residence-requirement community list. Do not price any parcel on STR income.
faq.q: Can I run a farm stay or short-term rental on a farm parcel?

faq.a: Only if a pair was legally split — as a 2-lot strata plan or by fee-simple subdivision. No named example of either form is verified here, and the A-1 (8 ha) and A-2 (16 ha) subdivision minimums mean farm lots here effectively cannot split into half-duplex parcels. Check title and plan before the form is believed.
faq.q: Can I buy half a duplex in West Meadows?

faq.a: In the RS pocket, one garden suite or one secondary suite per lot (33–90 sq m) — never both.
faq.q: What are the rules for farm houses and second homes here?

faq.a: Pitt Meadows Regional Airport (YPK), with three paved runways and a water runway, is inside this sub-area, so aircraft activity should be disclosed early and the City's airport page checked for the noise-concern process.
faq.q: Does the airport affect a purchase here?

faq.a: The City states the city is almost entirely protected by 60 km of dikes plus pump stations and flood boxes, and its 2020 Business Plan states over 95% of Pitt Meadows lies within the Fraser River and Pitt River floodplains; the Kennedy drainage area in this part of the city drains to the Alouette, Pitt and Fraser Rivers.
faq.q: Is West Meadows protected from flooding?
